headline: Am I living in her shadow?
note:
🔄 REWRITTEN 2026-08-19 to the Natural Tarot-Cut framework. Bubbles 3-6 now run as ONE causal chain — so / and / but / that's why — and the read ANSWERS instead of certifying her. The art line and the bridge are unchanged. Every family ban below still stands; this family was NOT loosened.

⚠️ "her" may be an EX or a woman who has DIED, and the headline does not say. 🔴 NEVER presume which. 🔴🔴 MEDIUMSHIP BAN (this family runs the decode-him frame, which carries none of it): never that she is at peace, watching, or would want anything. 🔴 NEVER disparage or characterise her, never make her a rival, never rank the two women. And the tightrope: never confirm the comparison as fact, never tell her she is imagining it.

VOC (769 V1 concerns, married-man/other-woman theme) settles why that tightrope is real: the other woman is very often NOT a rival — she is dead, ill, dependent, or entirely legitimate. "He lost his wife of 57 years a short while ago." "His wife is in bad health... I certainly would not hurt his wife." "I'm not a marriage breaker." Handing this reader an enemy would be harm dressed as comfort.

So the split, exactly as `hidden-intuition` splits its question: certify HER FEELING (she has felt something in the room) and refuse to rule on the woman at all. The finding does the rest — a shadow is not a person, it is what falls when something blocks the light. Which makes bubble 7 the easiest object on the funnel: the thing blocking the light IS the block Act 1 clears.

a: You turned the Magician, dear. Look — the number one sits at the very top of his card.
You asked if you're living in her shadow. Your hand went to the man who deals in solid things.
So there is something in that room with you, dear. The card gives you that.
And a shadow isn't a person, dear. It's what falls when the light is blocked.
But nobody has ever set out the terms, dear. You've been guessing at them.
That's why a good day with him can still end with you comparing, dear.
Let me look closer at what's standing between you and the light…
b: You turned the Hanged Man, dear. Look — his hands are tucked behind his back, out of sight.
You asked if you're living in her shadow. Your hand went to the man hung upside down.
So no measure was ever set out for you, dear. His hands are behind his back.
And the light in this comes from him, dear. He decides what gets shown.
But you can't answer a question that was never asked out loud, dear.
That's why you go looking for signs of her, dear, and you keep finding them.
Let me look closer at what's casting this over you…
c: You turned the Fool, dear. Look — mountains behind him, and one step left before the drop.
You asked if you're living in her shadow. Your hand went to the one who came in late.
So you came in after her, dear. Coming later doesn't put you under anyone.
And look at him, dear. He walks in with nothing settled and no past to carry.
But the order still gets treated like a ranking, dear. No one has said otherwise.
That's why the good days still leave you checking, dear. You've had no word to hold.
Let me look closer at what stands between you and being seen plainly…
